text: About 5,000 years ago, people built towns in three river valleys on the dry coast of Peru.
They built great stepped pyramids of earth and stone, but no walls or forts for war.
src: flourishing between about 3000 and 1800 BCE / a cluster of as many as thirty population centres in three small valleys of Peru’s north-central coast / Its coast is extremely dry
rectangular terraced pyramids / The builders used quarried stone and river cobbles / no fortifications, weapons, burned buildings or mutilated bodies from battle

text: Farmers in the valleys brought river water to their fields and grew cotton and food.
Fishers on the coast needed the cotton for their nets, and in return they gave fish to the farmers.
src: grew cotton and food crops by irrigation / Cotton, the chief product of irrigation
the people of the valleys needed fish for protein, and the fishers needed cotton to make their nets / Fish reached the inland sites, above all anchovies and sardines

text: They made no pottery and almost no paintings, but cloth mattered a lot to them.
A knotted string found at Caral may have been a quipu, a way of keeping records with knots.
src: There was no pottery at all / there is almost no sculpture, carving or painting / Cloth and textile technology mattered greatly
A knotted string found at Caral has been called a quipu, the recording device later perfected by the Inca / record-keeping with knots is older than had been thought

text: One baby at Caral was wrapped and buried with a necklace of stone beads.
The people also played flutes made from the bones of pelicans and condors.
src: a baby at Caral was wrapped and buried with a necklace of stone beads
The people of Caral–Supe made music. A temple at Caral held 32 flutes made of pelican and condor bone

text: Later a long drought, a time with little rain, drove people from Caral, and they built new towns elsewhere.
Today the archaeologist Ruth Shady still studies Caral–Supe, the oldest known civilisation of the Americas.
src: a long drought begins that later drives people from Caral / People of the Supe valley seem to have moved rather than collapsed, rebuilding at sites such as Vichama on the coast and Peñico inland
Ruth Shady’s research at Caral continues / It is the oldest known civilisation of the Americas
